A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework, models and applications. Text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–I support comparison; additions, relocations and renumbering can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical transferability tests and trained-model experiments on synthetic sets, graphs and ModelNet10 point clouds, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including model-output convergence, test MSE and prediction-versus-target plots in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The GGNN, continuous GGNN, SVD-DS and normalized/compatible DS-CI procedures are retained. Local equation corrections and the added explanation of how GGNN recovers an existing GNN do not establish a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four population-statistics tasks, maximum-distance task, weighted and stochastic-block-model graphs, and ModelNet10 chair/sofa point-cloud pairs. The added theoretical sampling corollaries introduce no evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: The comparator sets are unchanged in corresponding experiments, including DeepSet/PointNet, GNN/normalized 2-IGN and DS-CI comparisons. Corrections to the displayed IGN basis amend its mathematical description without establishing a different evaluated implementation.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain the same splits, sample counts, input sizes, model configurations, MSE evaluation and training budgets. Revised sampling assumptions elsewhere concern theoretical guarantees rather than experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The random-initialization transferability tests and appendix prediction-versus-target analyses are retained. New explanations of existing GGNN behavior add interpretation, without new ablation, robustness or case-study evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 100-sample standard-deviation reporting for untrained-model tests and the same repeated-training summaries. Min/max ranges, graph-result percentiles, and point-cloud trials selecting the best of five initializations are unchanged.

E6.justification: All empirical plot content is retained, including all 20 unique embedded plot streams. Matched curves, predictions, rankings and reported empirical findings are unchanged; v1 Figures 1–8 are renumbered around the new explanatory diagrams.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit sampling-rate corollaries E.6, F.4, G.3 and G.6 and a moment-matrix convergence argument for SVD-DS. It strengthens C.3's moment assumption to q > 2p, restricts Corollary G.1 to uniformly bounded inputs, and revises the orbit-space characterizations in E.1–E.2. Corrections also affect the graphon operator-distance bound, the covering-number factor in Equation (5), and displayed IGN basis formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introduction contributions retain the same claims: a general transferability framework, size-generalization guarantees, analysis of existing architectures, and construction of transferable graph and point-cloud models.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds discussion of the practicality of the assumptions. Appendix F distinguishes simple-graph convergence from weighted-graph behavior, offers an explanation for the retained GGNN plot, and states limitations involving higher-order IGN expressivity. These qualify particular applications; Appendix I's general limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access information, PyTorch implementation, NVIDIA A5000 hardware, optimizer settings, training schedules and runtime disclosures are retained. No new experimental reproduction instructions or resource availability changes are reported.

R1.justification: Related work expands to additional GNN generalization approaches, measure-to-measure architectures and transformer limit analyses. Appendix F substantially revises positioning: previously claimed recovery of random-graph convergence rates becomes a non-comparability qualification, and the speculative IWN critique is replaced with a more differentiated account of its guarantees and expressivity.

P1.justification: v2 adds terminology clarification, explanatory paragraphs and descriptive headings, particularly in Appendices D–G. The main narrative, section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: New Figures 1 and 3 illustrate consistent sequences and limit spaces for sets and graphs. Existing plots are retained with renumbering, caption wrapping and page reflow; the overall visual format and table structures remain similar.

improvement.justification: v2 narrows previously overbroad sampling and DS-CI guarantees, corrects mathematical expressions, and replaces speculative prior-work criticism with qualified comparisons. The diagrams also improve accessibility. These support a modest net improvement, although new Corollaries E.6 and G.6 do not consistently state C.3's stronger moment requirement, leaving gaps in the expanded rate claims.
